what: Names: Gosain, Sanniasi, Dasnami; a caste has developed out of orders of Sivite mendicants; Sadhu generic
quote: A name for the orders of religious mendicants of the Sivite sect, from which a caste has now developed.

what: Gosain in the CP means Sivite orders; contrasted with Bengal Bairagi/Vaishnava heads and Vallabhacharya Gokulastha Gosains
quote: But over most of India, as in the Central Provinces, Gosain appears to be a name applied to members of the Sivite orders.

what: Dasnami = ten names; Gosain now commonly applied to married caste members, mendicants called Sadhu or Sanniasi
quote: The name Gosain is now more commonly applied to the married members of the caste, who pursue ordinary avocations, while the mendicants are known as Sadhu or Sanniasi.

what: Founder Shankar Acharya (8th-10th c. per text) with four disciples; ten orders listed (Giri, Puri, Parbat, Sagar, Ban, Tirtha, Bharthi, Saraswati, Aranya, Ashram)
quote: The Gosains consider their founder to have been Shankar Acharya, the great apostle of the revival of the worship of Siva in southern India, who lived between the eighth and tenth centuries.

what: Orders assigned to four headquarters: Saraswati/Bharthi/Puri to Sringeri; Tirtha/Ashram to Dwarka; Ban/Aranya to Govardhan; Giri/Parbat/Sagara to Badrinath (outside CP)
quote: The Saraswati, Bharthi and Puri orders are supposed to be attached to the monastery at Sringeri in Mysore; the Tirtha and Ashram to that at Dwarka in Gujarat;

what: Dandi sometimes counted among ten orders but is a designation of staff-carrying ascetics from Tirtha, Ashram, Bharthi or Saraswati; Abdhut also used, esp. Dattatreya followers
quote: Dandi is sometimes shown as one of the ten orders, but it seems to be the special designation of certain ascetics who carry a staff

what: Commonest orders in CP: Giri, Puri, Bharthi (used as surnames); Aranya, Sagara, Parbat rarely met
quote: The commonest orders in the Central Provinces are Giri, Puri and Bharthi, and the members frequently use the name of the order as their surname.

what: Initiation open formerly to twice-born only; now any caste from which a Brahman takes water; Gonds and Kols said to be admitted locally; social fall; Giri said still Brahman-only
quote: Formerly only Brahmans or members of the twice-born castes could become Gosains, but now a man of any caste, as Kurmi, Kunbi or Mali, from whom a Brahman takes water, may be admitted.

what: Initiation rite: panchgavya cleansing, guru's toe-water and leavings, sacred thread broken, head shaved, mantra whispered in ear
quote: At initiation the body of a neophyte is cleaned with the five products of the sacred cow, milk, curds, ghi, dung and urine.

what: Dress and insignia: ochre cloth (Lal Padri vs white-clad Vaishnava Sita Padri), rudraksha rosary, tripundra ash marks, pilgrimage rings (Badrinath, Hinglaj, Rameshwaram)
quote: on this account they are called Lal Padri or red priest, while Vishnuite mendicants, who dress in white, are called Sita Padri.

what: Naga Gosains named for going naked into battle; famous fighting corps; formerly went naked at festivals
quote: The Naga Gosains, so called because they were once accustomed to go naked into battle, were a famous fighting corps.

what: Initiation on the Nerbudda: shorn hair thrown into the river; Narmada parikrama rules (about three years) and greeting 'Har Nerbudda'
quote: Those who are initiated on the banks of the Nerbudda throw the hair cut from their head into the sacred river.

what: Narmada circuit rules: no hair/nail cutting for about three years, not entering river above knees
quote: Those who are performing the perikrama or circuit of the Nerbudda from its source to its mouth and back, do not cut their hair or nails during the whole period of about three years.

what: Begging practices: cry Alakh; salutation 'Namu Narayan' answered 'Narayan' (text notes odd use of Vishnu's name)
quote: When an ordinary Hindu meets a Gosain he says 'Namu Narayan' or 'I go to Narayan,' and the Gosain answers 'Narayan.'

what: Dandis: special group across several orders; 12-year probation as Dandi before Sanniasi (one account) or Brahman-only (another); staff rules; rules disregarded in practice; no idol worship; 'Sevoham' (I am Siva)
quote: The Dandis are a special group of ascetics belonging to several of the ten orders.

what: Dandis and Sanniasis do not worship idols, being themselves part of the deity; formula 'Sevoham' (sic)
quote: Dandis and Sanniasis do not worship idols, as they are themselves considered to have become part of the deity.

what: Rawanvansi Gosains: class that goes about in the character of Rawan; hair rings, beg only at twilight
quote: Another curious class of Gosains are the Rawanvansis, who go about in the character of Rawan, the demon king of Ceylon, as he was when he carried off Sita.

what: Unmarried Sanniasis reside in maths under a Mahant who appoints successor by will; admits entrants; parental vows of children to the order
quote: Unmarried Sanniasis often reside in Maths or monasteries. The superior is called Mahant, and he appoints his successor by will from the members.

what: Many convents have considerable land attached and dependent institutions; Mahant has absolute disposal of property but must feed, clothe and lodge inmates and travellers of the order
quote: Many convents have considerable areas of land attached to them, and also dependent institutions.

what: Naga Gosains of Jaipur (7000) bound to fight for the Raja, rent-free lands, pay of two pice, vanguard; also lent money and took debtors' sons (not CP)
quote: They received rent-free lands and pay of two pice (1/2d.) a day, which latter was put into a common treasury and expended on the purchase of arms and ammunition whenever needed for war.

what: Jaipur Naga Gosains lent money and enrolled debtors' sons if unpaid
quote: They would also lend money, and if a debtor could not pay would make him give his son to be enrolled in the force.

what: Gosain proprietor of Deopur estate, Raipur, kept Naga Gosain force collecting tribute from Chhattisgarh feudatory chiefs for the Raja of Nagpur; invaded Bastar, many died of cholera; goddess Danteshwari taken to Deopur
quote: The Gosain proprietor of the Deopur estate in Raipur formerly kept up a force of Naga Gosains, with which he used to collect the tribute from the feudatory chiefs of Chhattisgarh on behalf of the Raja of Nagpur.

what: Deopur estate in Raipur held by a Gosain proprietor (landholder, Maratha-period tribute collector)
quote: The Gosain proprietor of the Deopur estate in Raipur formerly kept up a force of Naga Gosains

what: Gosain-Bairagi rivalry over first bathing at Ganges fairs; 1760 battle, 1800 Bairagis slain; 1796 Gosains defeated by Sikh pilgrims, 500 lost (not CP; from Nesfield)
quote: In 1760 a pitched battle on this question ended in the defeat of the Bairagis, of whom 1800 were slain.

what: Right of first bathing at great fairs disputed between Gosains (Siva) and Bairagis (Vishnu)
quote: A favourite point of rivalry was the right of bathing first in the Ganges on the occasion of one of the great religious fairs at Allahabad or Hardwar.

what: Akbar-era contest in which Gosains/Sanniasis defeated Jogis (Oman)
quote: During the reign of Akbar a combat took place in the Emperor's presence between the two Sivite sects of Gosains, or Sanniasis and Jogis

what: Burial: dead Sanniasi buried seated cross-legged with salt, staff, wallet, gourd; processions sometimes festive (Oman)
quote: A dead Sanniasi is always buried in the sitting attitude of religious contemplation with the legs crossed.

what: Celibacy the rule, property passes to chosen chela; keeping women very common; women admitted in some past; sons adopted as chelas by other Gosains by reciprocal arrangement; wandering mendicants' scandals
quote: Celibacy is the rule of the Gosain orders, and a man's property passes in inheritance to a selected chela or disciple.

what: Women who commit social offence or leave husbands often join the order nominally and live with a Gosain or are married into the caste
quote: Women who are convicted of some social offence, or who wish to leave their husbands, often join the order nominally and live with a Gosain or are married into the caste.

what: Wandering Gosains' reputation among villagers: ribald Gond Holi song about village women welcoming a Gosain
quote: a ribald Gond song sung at the Holi festival describes the pleasure of the village women at the arrival of a Gosain

what: Missionary role: wandering Gosains are gurus of middle and lower castes and largely responsible for converting aboriginal tribes to Hinduism
quote: They are the gurus or spiritual preceptors of the middle and lower castes

what: Same: formerly proselytised non-Aryan tribes in the wildest tracts, at risk of life
quote: In former times the Gosains travelled over the wildest tracts of country, proselytising the primitive non-Aryan tribes, for whose conversion to Hinduism they are largely responsible.

what: Majority now married and form an ordinary caste; Giri all marry; Bharthi may or may not; orders possibly exogamous groups (Buchanan, doubtful now)
quote: The majority of the Gosains are, however, now married and form an ordinary caste.

what: Caste customs: no first-cousin marriage; widow remarriage and divorce allowed; eat flesh of clean animals and fowl, drink liquor; take cooked food from higher castes incl. Sunars and Kunbis
quote: They prohibit any marriage between first cousins, but permit widow remarriage and divorce.

what: Social position: not high, Brahmans do not take water from them, but religious character gives prestige
quote: Hence they do not rank high socially, and Brahmans do not take water from them, but their religious character gives them some prestige.

what: Many Gosains became landholders through charitable grants from clients or moneylending; harsh landlords and grasping creditors
quote: Many Gosains have become landholders, obtaining their estates either as charitable grants from clients or through moneylending transactions.

what: Moneylending: Gosains considered grasping creditors
quote: In this capacity they do not usually turn out well, and are often considered harsh landlords and grasping creditors.

what: Jogi as order of Siva devotees following Yoga system of Patanjali
quote: The well-known order of religious mendicants and devotees of Siva.

what: 12 Panths venerating twelve disciples of Gorakhnath, names generally unknown; main divisions Kanphata and Aughar
quote: They are said to be divided into twelve Panths or orders, each of which venerates one of the twelve disciples of Gorakhnath.

what: Kanphatas pierce ears, rings; 12-year apprenticeship as Aughar; elite Darshani live in forest; names end Nath (Kanphata) / Das (Aughar)
quote: The names of the Kanphatas end in Nath and those of the Aughars in Das.

what: Jogi novice makes one or three Narmada parikramas during 12-year Brahmachari period; wears ochre like Sanniasis and all Sivite orders; Lal Padri
quote: During his twelve years' period as a Brahmachari or acolyte, a Jogi will make either one or three parikramas of the Nerbudda

what: Jogi burial: seated cross-legged, face north, tomb with recess like Muhammadans
quote: The Jogis are buried sitting cross-legged with the face to the north in a tomb which has a recess like those of Muhammadans.

what: Jogis worship Siva; Shivratri with songs to Gorakhnath; Nag-Panchmi cobra veneration
quote: The Jogis worship Siva, and their principal festival is the Shivratri, when they stay awake all night and sing songs in honour of Gorakhnath

what: Large part of Jogis became a caste of married people with occupational subcastes (Barwa/Garpagari, Manihari, Ritha Bikanath, Patbina, Ladaimar); low menial caste; Brahmans employed except Kanphatas
quote: These Jogis rank as a low Hindu caste of the menial group. No good Hindu caste will take food or water from them

what: Begging traditional; Kanphatas sell ganda amulets, cry Alakh; Nandia Jogis with deformed ox; many secular occupations (pedlars, conjuring, Saugor card tricks, swindling)
quote: Begging is the traditional occupation of the Jogis, but they have now adopted many others.
